story.title: Codenaut
story.text:
Long ago, the planets in this part of space were bright and colorful: houses in every color, giant and tiny stars, neat borders around every little house. But cosmic disasters struck the planets — star storms, meteor showers — and wiped out all the magic words-commands.

Your ship found the first planet in trouble. You are the only one who knows how to find the lost words-commands and write them again.

Sit down at the controls, write the commands, and watch the planet come alive right before your eyes. Save one planet — the path opens to the next.

Ready? Let's fly and save the cosmos!
story.bookHint: You can go through the welcome again here and refresh how it all works.

colors/01-ball-color.text: {{name}} bought a ball on the Colors planet, but the seller mixed it up and gave a grey one. Make the ball [[green]].
colors/01-ball-color.teachBody: [[background-color]] paints the inside of a shape. It is written like this: a name, then a colon, then the colour. A colon is the sign that says "and here is the value". The colour you need here is called [[green]].
hints: You need to paint the shape, not the text. Remember which property paints the inside of a shape — its name is already written in the editor.
colors/01-ball-color.success: Great job! The ball is green.

colors/02-color-too-dark.text: {{name}} found an old sign on the Colors planet. The letters are almost black, so you can hardly read them. Make the letters [[white]].
colors/02-color-too-dark.teachBody: [[color]] paints the letters. Its name is already written in the editor. After the colon write the colour the letters need — here they have to be [[white]].
hints: The letters are too dark to read. They need to be light instead — the colour for that is called [[white]].
colors/02-color-too-dark.success: Great job! Now the sign can be read.

colors/03-pick-background.text: {{name}} landed at night, but the sky is still grey and bright. Make the sky [[darkblue]].
colors/03-pick-background.teachBody: The sky is a shape too — a very big one. Drag the property that paints the inside of a shape into the editor: it comes with its colour already written, and that colour is called [[darkblue]].
hints: The sky is a shape, and you need the property that paints the inside of a shape. Its name is in the basket.
colors/03-pick-background.success: Great job! It is night on this planet.

colors/04-pick-border.text: {{name}} found the school sign, but its frame is dark grey and easy to miss. Make the frame [[yellow]].
colors/04-pick-border.teachBody: The frame around a shape is called its border, and there is a property [[border-color]] that paints only that frame. Drag its name from the basket into the editor — it brings the [[yellow]] with it.
hints: You are not painting the inside this time, and not the letters — the frame around the sign. The property with border in its name does that.
colors/04-pick-border.success: Great job! That sign is impossible to miss now.

colors/05-color-combo.text: {{name}} wants a real Codenaut badge: the inside [[blue]], the frame [[yellow]], the letters [[white]]. Three commands!
colors/05-color-combo.teachBody: You already know all three. One command paints the inside, one paints the frame, one paints the letters. And the colours are familiar ones: inside [[blue]], frame [[yellow]], letters [[white]]. Write each on its own line, and end every command with a semicolon.
hints: Check the badge part by part: the inside, the frame, the letters. Two of them may already be right — look at the third.
colors/05-color-combo.success: Great job! That is a real Codenaut badge.

sizes/01-how-wide.text: {{name}} found a door on the Sizes planet, but it is too narrow to walk through. Make the door 160 pixels wide.
sizes/01-how-wide.teachBody: [[width]] says how wide a shape is. Its name is already written in the editor. After the colon write how many pixels wide it should be: a number, then px.
hints: You want the door to be wide, not tall. Write the number you want and add px after it.
sizes/01-how-wide.success: Great job! The door is wide enough now.

sizes/02-how-tall.text: {{name}} found a rocket, but it is squashed and almost flat. Make the rocket 180 pixels tall.
sizes/02-how-tall.teachBody: [[height]] says how tall a shape is. Its name is already written in the editor. Heights are written in pixels too: a number, then px.
hints: The rocket has to be tall, not wide. You want the command whose name means [[height]].
sizes/02-how-tall.success: Great job! That rocket is ready to fly.

sizes/03-pick-height.text: {{name}} is at the base of the Sizes planet, but the window is squashed. Make the window 160 pixels tall.
sizes/03-pick-height.teachBody: One name in the basket makes a shape wide and one makes it tall. Drag the one that makes the window 160 pixels tall — the number comes with it.
hints: Read the task: the window has to be tall, not wide. Pick the name that means tall.
sizes/03-pick-height.success: Great job! You can see out of that window.

sizes/04-make-round.text: {{name}} found a planet that is square. Real planets are round. Round its corners by 60 pixels to make it a circle.
sizes/04-make-round.teachBody: [[border-radius]] says how much the corners of a shape are rounded. Half of the size is enough to make a circle, and on this 120-pixel planet the command brings 60px. Drag it in — and if you like, change the 60px to 50%, it means the same half.
hints: The corners need rounding. One of the names in the basket is the one about rounding.
sizes/04-make-round.success: Great job! That is a round planet.

sizes/05-size-combo.text: {{name}} wants a round portal: 140 pixels wide, 140 pixels tall. Three commands at once!
sizes/05-size-combo.teachBody: You know them from the first tasks. Their names are [[width]], [[height]] and [[border-radius]]. Three commands, one per line, each ending with a semicolon. A circle needs as many pixels across as it is tall.
hints: Take it part by part: first the [[width]], then the [[height]], then the [[border-radius]]. Half of the [[width]] is how much a circle needs.
sizes/05-size-combo.success: Great job! The portal is open.
